issues.legal_issue: The period for making an award in a land acquisition runs from the last completed mode of publication of the declaration, and the acquisition proceedings lapse if the award is not made within the applicable period after excluding time during which the proceedings were stayed by a court.
material_facts: The declaration was published through the prescribed modes, and the record established that the last relevant publication occurred on 25 July 1985; the notice dated 13 August 1985 concerned taking possession and did not establish a later publication of the declaration.
The award challenged by the landowners was made on 18 September 1998.
The acquisition proceedings were stayed from 2 August 1985 until the Supreme Court decided the earlier appeals on 19 September 1996.
Even after excluding the period of the court stay, the award was not made within the statutory period.
issues.conclusion: The award was beyond the permissible period, so the acquisition proceedings had lapsed; the High Court’s contrary judgment was set aside and the landowners’ writ petitions were allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, publication in the Official Gazette, publication in two qualifying daily newspapers, and public notice of the substance of the declaration in the locality are conjoint and cumulative requirements. The date of publication for Section 11A is the last date among those modes, and the period for making the award runs from that date, excluding any period during which action or proceedings pursuant to the declaration were stayed by a court. The Court relied on Krishi Utpadan Mandi Samiti v. Markant Singh, Eugenio Misquita v. State of Goa, General Manager, Department of Telecommunications v. Jacob, and Bihar State Housing Board v. State of Bihar; it distinguished State of Haryana v. Raghubir Dayal as not assisting the respondents.

rule.if: land_acquisition_award_challenge and declaration_published_through_required_modes and final_declaration_publication_preceded_award and acquisition_proceedings_stayed_by_court and award_exceeded_permitted_time_after_stay_exclusion

predicates.land_acquisition_award_challenge: The case is a challenge to an award made in land acquisition proceedings.
predicates.declaration_published_through_required_m: The acquiring authority published the declaration through the required publication methods.
predicates.final_declaration_publication_preceded_a: The last required publication of the declaration occurred before the award was made.
predicates.acquisition_proceedings_stayed_by_court: A court stayed action or proceedings taken pursuant to the declaration for a period before the award was made.
predicates.award_exceeded_permitted_time_after_stay: After accounting for the period of the court stay, the award was still made later than the permitted time measured from the last required publication.

issues.definition: When an award challenge concerns a declaration published through the required methods and the award was made beyond the permitted time measured from the final publication after excluding court-stay time, the acquisition proceedings lapse.

issues.legal_issue: A contempt petition alleging breach of a status quo order is not established where the record does not show that the respondents wilfully or intentionally violated the order.
material_facts: The Supreme Court had ordered that possession remain in status quo while the appeal was pending.
The landowners alleged that development authority officials encroached on land and demolished a boundary wall and cattle sheds despite the order.
The respondents denied disturbing the status quo and stated that work had been carried out on a different plot outside the order’s scope.
After considering the parties’ affidavits, the Court found no evidence that the respondents had wilfully or intentionally violated the order.
issues.conclusion: The Court found that this was not a fit case for contempt proceedings, disposed of the contempt petition, and discharged the notice.
issues.legal_principle: The Court’s application of contempt jurisdiction required evidence of wilful flouting or intentional violation of its order. It cited no statute or earlier case for this determination.

predicates.contempt_petition_concerning_status_quo_: A party brought a contempt petition alleging breach of a court order requiring possession to remain unchanged.
predicates.respondents_denied_disturbing_ordered_st: The respondents denied changing the condition of the property covered by the order and said their work concerned other property.
predicates.record_lacked_evidence_of_wilful_or_inte: The materials before the court did not establish that the respondents deliberately or wilfully breached the order.

issues.definition: When a contempt petition concerns a status quo order, the respondents deny disturbing the protected status, and the record lacks evidence of wilful or intentional violation, contempt is not established.
